sources.title: Current president biography: earlier cabinet roles, Petrobras board chair and 2014 BRICS cooperation
sources.findings: Read NDB’s current president biography. Rousseff is President of the Bank, not chair of its Board of Governors. Earlier posts include Brazil’s minister of mines and energy, presidential chief of staff and Petrobras board chair; board chair is not the company CEO. The biography records participation with other BRICS governments in the July 2014 founding process. Its positive claims about poverty reduction, economic stability and the UN Hunger Map are institutional biographical assessments, not independent causal findings reproduced in this dossier. Do not turn two electoral victories into two completed presidential terms.

sources.title: 19 March 2025 re-election for the term 7 July 2025 to 6 July 2030
sources.findings: Read NDB’s re-election release. The Board of Governors unanimously elected her on 19 March 2025 for a term from 7 July 2025 to 6 July 2030. Election date, effective term start and planned term endpoint are separate. Current November 2026 evidence corroborates continued office; a scheduled 2030 endpoint is not a claim that she has already served through it. No unsupported claim that she personally appoints the governors or controls the bank without board oversight.

sources.title: 24 March 2023 election as president, effective immediately
sources.findings: Read the 24 March 2023 election release. It explicitly says effective immediately and identifies the President as chief of the operating staff conducting ordinary business under the Directors’ direction. This is the original start date, despite later public welcoming/inauguration coverage in April. Historical institutional membership statements are not reused as a current member list; the release’s praise and future goals are not completed project outcomes.

sources.title: 12 November 2026 report: exchange at COP31 about a just energy transition and technology
sources.findings: Read Instituto E+ Transição Energética’s report dated 12 November 2026. It describes her receiving the institute’s research booklet during COP31 in Antalya and quotes her emphasis on a just energy transition together with technology. The report date is not a verified exact meeting or recording time. This is the host organisation’s textual account of an actual exchange; no video was watched and no claim is made that she authored, financed, approved or implemented the institute’s reports. A planned COP31 agenda launch is not recorded as completed.

sources.title: 6 November 2026: address at the ninth Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai
sources.findings: Read NDB’s photo-gallery text explicitly recording that she addressed the ninth Hongqiao International Economic Forum in Shanghai on 6 November 2026. This is a completed-activity caption, not a future event listing. Its stated financial-partnership theme is not a new treaty, approved loan or measured economic result. The gallery’s image pixels and full speech video were not inspected; role and activity are supported by its text.

sources.title: Former-president record: birth, first inauguration and presidential term ranges
sources.findings: Read the Presidency’s former-president record. It confirms birth on 14 December 1947 in Belo Horizonte, inauguration on 1 January 2011, first term ending 31 December 2014, and second term from 1 January 2015 to 31 August 2016. The second-term inauguration row mistakenly repeats 1 January 2011, contrary to its own term heading; the repeated date is not adopted. The page also says she was 63 at the 31 October 2010 election, whereas the given birth date implies 62 until December; omit that age claim. The older presidential-library URL returned 502, so the readable government successor record is the source used.

sources.title: Biographical record associated with the 16 June 2016 session: birth and 1977 economics graduation
sources.findings: Read the Bahia legislative biographical record associated with a 16 June 2016 honours session. It confirms her birth date and UFRGS economics graduation in 1977. Its statement that she studied at Unicamp is not proof of awarded master’s or doctoral degrees, and its compressed 1978 postgraduate wording does not establish both programmes’ start dates. Its then-prospective 2015–2018 presidential mandate is superseded by the actual August 2016 removal. Honorifics and honours are not academic research degrees.

sources.title: 10 July 2009: Unicamp clarification that postgraduate study did not result in master’s or doctoral degrees
sources.findings: Read Jornal do Brasil’s 10 July 2009 report of Unicamp’s clarification, attributed to Folha reporting. It explicitly distinguishes enrolment in master’s and doctoral programmes from completion of the required theses and defences; neither degree was obtained. An earlier university statement denying even master’s enrolment was corrected. This is a secondary account of the university statement, not direct inspection of academic records. Conflicting cancellation/abandonment years in reporting are not fixed as verified dates in the display text.

sources.publisher: Fundação Getulio Vargas, Atlas Histórico do Brasil
sources.title: Historical biography: political imprisonment, graduation, energy policy, Casa Civil and PAC
sources.findings: Read the relevant FGV Atlas biography sections on early activism, January 1970 arrest, torture in detention, release at the end of 1972, the 1977 undergraduate degree, energy administration, Casa Civil and PAC. It distinguishes membership in organisations advocating armed struggle from personal participation in military actions; group actions are not assigned to her. Its national-archive counterpart search excerpt gives 1969 for arrest, but FGV’s explicit 1970 chronology agrees with the Chamber biography and is used. Luz para Todos involved the ministry, Eletrobras, utilities and rural electrification cooperatives. PAC was a government programme with implementation partners and contested priorities; no personal authorship of all projects or guaranteed growth is inferred.

sources.title: 31 December 2010 biography: route to the presidency and earlier cabinet responsibilities
sources.findings: Read the Chamber of Deputies’ 31 December 2010 biography. It identifies national energy leadership from 2003 and the move to Casa Civil in 2005, succeeding José Dirceu, with government policy coordination and PAC responsibilities. Casa Civil is a cabinet office attached to the presidency, not a prime ministership. The article is historical: its pre-inauguration language, past health reporting and character assessments are not used as current facts. Its hedged historical torture wording is supported by FGV’s explicit account; no current medical status is asserted.

sources.title: 31 August 2016: removal from the presidency and separate vote preserving political rights
sources.findings: Read the Senate’s 31 August 2016 report. Removal passed by 61–20 over three supplementary-credit decrees without legislative approval and delayed Plano Safra subsidy transfers to Banco do Brasil. A separate public-office disqualification vote had 42 in favour, 36 against and three abstentions, falling short of the required 54. Preserve the distinction between removal and failure to impose disqualification; 42 did not vote to preserve rights. The text calls 54 an absolute majority, which is imprecise for an 81-member Senate; no such label is repeated. This impeachment proceeding for crime de responsabilidade is not a personal-bribery conviction, prison sentence or loss of all political rights.

sources.title: 29 August 2016: Rousseff’s defence statement denying an impeachable offence and alleging a coup
sources.findings: Read the Chamber’s contemporaneous 29 August 2016 report of her defence statement. She denied committing an impeachable offence and described the proceeding as a coup. Her legal and political position is attributed, not treated as a judicial reversal or an established neutral label for the process. Her assertions about others’ misconduct and personal wealth are not reproduced as independently established facts. The statement precedes the final 31 August vote.

sources.title: General Strategy 2017–2021, Box 1: founding agreement signed 15 July 2014, effective 3 July 2015
sources.findings: Read the executive-summary timing and Box 1, Trajectory of NDB’s Creation, on PDF page 9 of the bank’s 2017–2021 strategy. Five founding governments signed the agreement on 15 July 2014; it entered into force on 3 July 2015, followed by the inaugural governors’ meeting on 7 July. Preserve multilateral contribution and signature versus entry into force versus operational launch. The executive summary misnumbers the Fortaleza summit as the fifth, so no summit ordinal is copied. The document is a historical strategy, not current 2026 targets; the full strategy was not reviewed. The 2018 annual-report PDF could not be opened because of tool size limits.

sources.title: 13 April 2023: Lula’s visit to the Shanghai headquarters and Rousseff’s statement
sources.findings: Read NDB’s record of Lula’s 13 April 2023 visit to the Shanghai headquarters, including Rousseff’s statement and the stated purpose of cooperation. This is a later public event, distinct from her immediately effective 24 March election. No video was watched. Institutional claims about ending poverty and advancing sustainability are aims, not measured achievements attributed to her alone.

portraitReview.credit: Vice-Presidência da República (VPR) / Divulgação VPR; cropped by Cataleirxs
portraitReview.unresolved: Read candidate and parent Commons pages plus the original VPR Flickr description. Flickr identifies a 4 June 2024 Beijing meeting with Geraldo Alckmin concerning a commitment letter for Rio Grande do Sul resources; a commitment letter is not proof of disbursement. Flickr capture/upload date is 4 June; the parent was transferred by Yacàwotçã and licence-reviewed by FlickreviewR 2 on 17 July; Cataleirxs cropped it on 24 July. Preserve those separate roles and dates. Candidate metadata is 1199×1596 and parent 4000×2666. The Flickr rights link resolves directly to CC BY 2.0, matching Commons; preserve institutional credit and crop attribution rather than inventing a named photographer. Original download on 18 November failed with curl 22, HTTP 403 and reported HTTP 000; referenced cache is absent. Full bytes, identity, colour and crop suitability remain visually unverified.

remainingWork: Download and inspect the original portrait for identity, colour and crop suitability, retaining VPR/Divulgação VPR and Cataleirxs attribution under CC BY 2.0.
Recheck current NDB leadership and newer actual activity before publication; future appointments, planned terms, financing commitments and organisational impact claims require distinct evidence.
